title: Roll a drum up a ramp onto a deck
instruction: Roll the orange drum up the blue ramp onto the grey deck until it rests against the yellow stop bar, then move both arms at least 3 cm away from it.
context: Drums and reels too heavy to lift are rolled up skids or a ramp onto a dock or truck bed. The load runs back the moment the push stops, and it skews off the ramp if one end gets ahead.
setup: World frame: x forward from the arms, y to the robot's left, z up; positions are object centres; heights are above the table top, which is 74.75 cm above the floor. Table: fixed flat tabletop, oak-coloured wood, 110 x 130 x 6 cm, spanning x -0.19 to 0.91 m and y -0.65 to 0.65 m. Drum: loose smooth plastic drum, a closed orange cylinder 20 cm across and 26 cm long, 2.0 kg, with one dark grey stripe 1.5 cm wide painted along its whole length, lying on its side with its axis along y, centred at x 0.23, y 0, resting on the table (axis 10.1 cm up), the stripe on top. Ramp: fixed blue-painted steel plate 50 cm wide (y), 1.2 cm thick and 11.4 cm long along its slope, pitched 15.3 degrees, its top surface meeting the table at x 0.34 and the deck top at x 0.45; its lower end sits in the table. Deck: fixed light grey block 21 cm (x) by 50 cm (y) by 3 cm tall, from x 0.45 to 0.66, centred on y 0, its top 3 cm above the table, flush with the ramp's top. Stop bar: fixed yellow bar 2 cm (x) by 50 cm (y) by 3 cm tall standing on the deck along its far edge, from x 0.64 to 0.66; a drum on the deck rolled against it has its centre at x 0.569. Arms: two YAM 6-joint arms with parallel-jaw grippers (94 mm maximum opening, less than the drum's width), metal and plastic links, rubber-like finger pads, bases at x 0, y +-0.305 m, z 0.75 m, starting in the ready pose with the grippers open. Camera stand: fixed mock stand behind the arms, foot 11 x 11 x 1.6 cm centred at x -0.236, y -0.009 m on the table, 2.4 cm mast; the top camera and two wrist cameras are the adapter's station cameras. Nothing else is on the table. Friction: the drum's surface is 0.25 static and 0.20 dynamic against everything; all other contacts use the adapter's material, 1.2 static and 1.0 dynamic.
scoring: Scored at the end from a top photo and a tape measure; one rule is watched over the whole trial from the video. On the deck: the drum's lowest point is within 5 mm of the deck top, its centre is over the deck at least 5 cm past the ramp's top edge (x 0.50 to 0.64) and within 4 cm of the deck's centre line, and its axis is within 15 degrees of the stop bar's direction. Clear: no part of either arm is within 3 cm of the drum's surface (in simulation, measured on the arms' collision meshes, every link but the fixed base; a point on a mesh face between vertices is not measured). Still: the drum moves under 1 cm/s and turns under 0.5 rad/s, by the simulator's velocities. Lifted: at any control step (20 Hz) the drum's centre is more than 1.5 cm higher than it is when rolling on the surface under its centre (the table, the ramp or the deck top); once this happens the trial scores 0 whatever follows. 1.0, and the trial ends on that step: on the deck, still and clear together for 1 s (20 consecutive control steps), never lifted. 0.5: on the deck at the end, never lifted, but held or still moving. 0.25: never lifted, not on the deck, and its centre at least 1.5 cm higher than at the start, which is the drum held partway up the ramp or resting on the deck's edge. 0: anything else, including the drum off the ramp's side, back on the table, or off the table. The adapter's settling steps before the first control step are not evaluated.
reset_notes: Put the drum back at its start on the table with its axis along y, and both arms in the ready pose. Nothing is consumed.
fidelity: Rigid bodies in PhysX on CPU; the drum is a convex-mesh cylinder with no rolling resistance. Its friction is 0.25/0.20 with everything (PhysX combine 'min'), below measured plastics: with the adapter's 1.2 the rear of the rolling drum, which moves upwards, dragged the pushing hand up over it through the arm's soft joints. Ramp, deck and stop are fixed boxes. One fixed layout. The arms' clearance and the step count come from a wrapper on the adapter's scene module.
